name: Synthetic V2X 3D Semantic Occupancy Benchmark
description: 3D semantic occupancy prediction is an emerging perception paradigm in autonomous driving, providing a voxel-level representation of both geometric details and semantic categories. However, its effectiveness is inherently constrained in single-vehicle setups by occlusions, restricted sensor range, and narrow viewpoints. To address these limitations, collaborative perception enables the exchange of complementary information, thereby enhancing the completeness and accuracy of predictions. Despite its potential, research on collaborative 3D semantic occupancy prediction is hindered by the lack of dedicated datasets. To bridge this gap, we design a high-resolution semantic voxel sensor in CARLA to produce dense and comprehensive annotations. We further develop a baseline model that performs inter-agent feature fusion via spatial alignment and attention aggregation. In addition, we establish benchmarks with varying prediction ranges designed to systematically assess the impact of spatial extent on collaborative prediction. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of our baseline, with increasing gains observed as range expands. Our code is available at https://github.com/tlab-wide/Co3SOP}{https://github.com/tlab-wide/Co3SOP.
evaluation_method: voxel-level metrics (mean Intersection over Union / IoU per class), and voxel-wise classification metrics
general_score_metric: mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) over voxels/classes
notes: Synthetic CARLA-based dataset for collaborative V2X perception (non-LLM). Being simulated, there is a sim-to-real gap; benchmark emphasizes multi-agent fusion and large-range occupancy which may not directly transfer to real-world sensors. New benchmark with limited external adoption so far.
